chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked, while I was present, about a man who had become junub in his garment and then perspired in it,
He said: I do not see any problem with it.
He said: He sweats so much that, if he wished to wring it out, he could wring it out.
He said: So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام frowned and said: If you insist, then sprinkle it with a little water.
ai.seo_question: Is the sweat of a junub on clothing considered problematic in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on the sweat of a person in janabah affecting a garment. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in it, and when pressed further, he recommends sprinkling some water on the garment if they insist.
